title: Phase-Controlled Majorana Zero Modes in Altermagnetic Topological-Insulator Josephson Junctions
authors: Hao Dong, Xun-Jiang Luo, Xiao-Hong Pan, Xin Liu
abstract: We exploit facet-dependent Andreev phase shifts to control topological superconductivity with a phase bias in a three-dimensional altermagnetic topological-insulator Josephson junction. In the weak link between two conventional s-wave superconductors, the d-wave altermagnetic order produces facet-dependent momentum shifts of the surface Dirac cones. The resulting net momentum of the states involved in Andreev reflection generates additional propagation phases that differ between facets. Consequently, the facet-resolved Andreev spectra exhibit gap closings at distinct phase biases, giving rise to topological superconducting regimes that host Majorana zero modes(MZMs). We further show that tuning the phase bias controls the spatial localization of these modes. The associated topological superconducting transitions are only weakly affected by moderate variations in the chemical potential, obviating the need for fine-tuning to the Dirac point. Our results establish a platform for realizing and spatially controlling MZMs by tuning the superconducting phase bias in altermagnetic topological-insulator Josephson junctions.
summary: This theoretical work demonstrates how the d-wave altermagnetic order in a topological insulator creates distinct electronic properties on different crystal facets. By coupling this material into a Josephson junction, the authors show that tuning the superconducting phase bias can induce a superconducting mass inversion at the crystal hinges, thereby realizing and spatially controlling Majorana zero modes.
main_problem: The research aims to exploit facet-dependent Andreev phase shifts to control topological superconductivity in a Josephson junction formed by an altermagnetic topological insulator.
main_result: The study establishes a mechanism where the altermagnetic order induces distinct phase responses on different crystal facets, leading to a superconducting mass inversion at the facet hinges that hosts Majorana zero modes (MZMs).
method: The analysis involves deriving low-energy effective Hamiltonians by projecting the full lattice model onto the surface-state subspace and analyzing the resulting Andreev bound-state quantization conditions.
model_or_system: The system is a Josephson junction (SC/AMTI/SC) where the AMTI is modeled using a Hamiltonian incorporating d-wave altermagnetic order. The physics is analyzed by examining the Andreev spectra and the resulting superconducting gap structure.
key_observables: Facet-dependent gap closings in Andreev spectra, spatial localization of MZMs, and the sign change of the effective superconducting mass across crystal facets.
important_parameters: Superconducting phase bias ($\phi$), altermagnetic coupling strength ($t_J$), and the chemical potential ($\mu$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on projecting the full Hamiltonian onto the low-energy surface-state subspace and retaining only the leading low-energy Dirac expansion for the final bound-state expressions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of anisotropic AMTI surface states showing facet-dependent Dirac-cone shifts, and the Josephson junction setup with phase difference $\phi$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first modeling the AMTI surface states, showing how the altermagnetic term causes momentum shifts on lateral facets but not on top/bottom facets. It then applies this to the Josephson junction, deriving the phase-dependent Andreev spectra and demonstrating that the resulting mass inversion at the hinges hosts MZMs.
why_interesting: The ability to engineer topological superconductivity and control MZMs using geometric/structural properties (facets) and external biases ($\phi$) is highly relevant for realizing fault-tolerant quantum computing platforms.
